name: Argentina

C.evidence: Among the most intense national-team followings anywhere: 'Muchachos' singing sections, large travelling support in Qatar 2022 and across the 2026 host cities, loyal through the 2014-2021 trophy drought.

V.evidence: FIFA sanctioned the AFA for discriminatory chants in June 2025 (Argentina v Colombia, CHF 120,000, 25% spectator reduction) and again on 21 Aug 2026 (USD 321,000 for discriminatory chants/gestures, team misconduct, a political banner and security failures at the World Cup; two home matches at 50%, one suspended). Players were filmed singing a racist chant about France's players after the 2024 Copa America; four Argentina players/officials face assault/unsporting-behaviour proceedings after the 2026 final.

H.evidence: Three-time world champion (1978, 1986, 2022), runner-up 2026, 16 Copa Americas; Maradona 1986 and Messi's 2022 title are among the game's defining moments.

O.evidence: AFA president Claudio Tapia and senior officials formally charged in a tax-evasion case (asset freeze of 350m pesos); separate money-laundering probe around Sur Finanzas with more than 30 raids, including AFA headquarters (Dec 2025).

S.evidence: Scaloni in charge since 2018 (World Cup 2022, Copa 2021/2024, 2026 final); hard-running collective built around Messi, who retired from the national team after the 2026 World Cup. Stable core (Romero, Mac Allister, E. Fernandez, Martinez); Scaloni's contract runs to Dec 2026 with an extension under discussion.

adjustments.evidence: Repeated FIFA discrimination sanctions: CHF 120,000 plus partial closure (June 2025 qualifier) and USD 321,000 plus 50% capacity for two home matches (Aug 2026, World Cup chants/gestures); 2024 Copa America squad racist chant (FIFA probe).

Freedom House 2026: Free, 85/100, but RSF 2026 rank 98/180 (down 11 places; more than 69 places since 2022) over institutional hostility to the press and violence against journalists covering protests.

wc2026: runner-up (lost 1-0 to Spain in the final; beat Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland, England)

C.evidence: Huge global following, but home national-team crowds are often subdued and commentary in Brazil has described a disconnect between the Selecao and its public; no organised national-team singing culture comparable to its clubs.

V.evidence: No FIFA discrimination sanction found in the 2026 cycle; warning and CHF 5,000 fine for a pitch invasion (Brazil v Paraguay, June 2025). CBF has run anti-racism campaigns (Vinicius Junior). Neutral start.

H.evidence: Five-time world champion, only nation at every World Cup; Pele, 1970, 'jogo bonito' - central to the game's history.

O.evidence: President Ednaldo Rodrigues removed by a Rio court in May 2025 over a forged signature; Samir Xaud elected unopposed amid a club boycott. Three previous presidents (Teixeira, Marin, Del Nero) were banned or convicted in the FIFA corruption cases.

S.evidence: High coach churn after 2022 (Tite, interim Diniz, Dorival, Ancelotti from 2025, contract to 2030); round-of-16 exit to Norway, first since 1990. Individual stars (Vinicius, Raphinha), no settled collective identity yet.

name: Colombia

C.evidence: Loud yellow-shirted support at the Metropolitano in Barranquilla and very large travelling crowds in the US (Copa America 2024, World Cup 2026).

V.evidence: FIFA discrimination sanction June 2025 (Colombia v Peru: CHF 70,000, prevention plan, 25% spectator reduction). Ticketless fans forced entry at the 2024 Copa America final in Miami; federation president arrested there (charges dropped, son charged).

H.evidence: 1990s golden generation (Valderrama, Higuita, 5-0 in Buenos Aires 1993), 2001 Copa America, James Rodriguez's 2014 Golden Boot; 1994 killing of Andres Escobar.

O.evidence: Colombia's competition authority (SIC) fined the FCF and senior officials including president Ramon Jesurun about 18bn pesos over a 2018-qualifier ticket-resale scheme (upheld by the Cundinamarca tribunal). Jesurun arrested at the 2024 Copa final after a clash with security (charges dropped).

S.evidence: Nestor Lorenzo in charge since 2022, extended after the World Cup; 28-match unbeaten run 2022-24, Copa 2024 final; conceded one goal in five 2026 matches. Captain James Rodriguez and Luis Diaz as icons; stable squad.

adjustments.evidence: FIFA Article 15 (discrimination) sanction, Colombia v Peru, 6 June 2025: CHF 70,000 and partial closure.
Mass gate-crashing and crowd disorder by ticketless fans at the 2024 Copa America final (Hard Rock Stadium), dozens arrested including the federation president (charges later dropped).
Freedom House 2026: Free but only 69/100 (history of violence and rights abuses); RSF 2026 rank 102/180.

wc2026: round of 16 (lost to Switzerland on penalties after 0-0; beat Ghana 1-0 in round of 32)

C.evidence: Passionate home support at altitude in Quito's Rodrigo Paz Delgado/Atahualpa; solid but smaller travelling following.

V.evidence: FIFA fined Ecuador for fans' homophobic chants at the 2022 World Cup opener; CHF 11,000 fine for misconduct and fireworks (Ecuador v Brazil, June 2025). Byron Castillo eligibility case: fine and a 3-point deduction in 2026 qualifying.

H.evidence: Five World Cups since 2002; round of 16 in 2006; no senior titles.

O.evidence: FEF was sanctioned (fine, points deduction) over false documents for Byron Castillo; frequent coach changes (Alfaro, Sanchez, Beccacece, now Marcelo Gallardo).

S.evidence: Beccacece's high-intensity pressing side (2024-26) with an elite defence (Hincapie, Pacho) and Caicedo; beat Germany in the group; Beccacece left after the round-of-32 exit, Gallardo appointed.

adjustments.evidence: FIFA fine for discriminatory (homophobic) chants at the 2022 World Cup opener v Qatar.
Freedom House 2026: Partly Free, 64/100 (organised crime, due-process concerns under repeated states of emergency); RSF 2026 rank 125/180.

name: Paraguay

C.evidence: Loyal, loud support at Defensores del Chaco; strong following returned with the first World Cup since 2010.

V.evidence: No FIFA discrimination sanctions found this cycle. Neutral start, slightly lowered for a federation culture historically tied to CONMEBOL's Asuncion-based corruption (Leoz, Napout).

H.evidence: Nine World Cups, quarter-final 2010, Copa America 1953 and 1979, Chilavert era.

O.evidence: APF under Robert Harrison since 2019, stable; former APF president Juan Angel Napout convicted in the FIFA corruption case (2017).

S.evidence: Gustavo Alfaro since 2024, extended to 2030; compact, hard-working side that beat Germany on penalties and lost only 1-0 to France.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: Partly Free, 63/100 (corruption, organised crime, pressure on journalists); RSF 2026 rank 88/180.

wc2026: round of 16 (lost 1-0 to France; beat Germany on penalties in round of 32)

name: Uruguay

C.evidence: Fervent support from a nation of 3.4m; Estadio Centenario, strong 'garra charrua' identity and loyal travelling fans.

V.evidence: Players climbed into the stands at the 2024 Copa America semi-final (CONMEBOL bans incl. Darwin Nunez); FIFA sanctions after 2022 World Cup player abuse of officials; warning and CHF 2,500 fine in June 2025. No recent discrimination sanction found.

H.evidence: Two World Cups (1930 host, 1950 Maracanazo), two Olympic titles, 15 Copa Americas; foundational nation of international football.

O.evidence: AUF has a history of conflict with the players' union and the TV rights holder; ordinary governance, no current criminal case found.

S.evidence: Bielsa era (2023-26) ended with a group-stage exit and public splits (Suarez's 2024 criticism of the dressing room); Diego Forlan interim coach. Federico Valverde as current icon.

wc2026: group stage (2 points: Spain, Cape Verde, Saudi Arabia)

name: Mexico

C.evidence: Very large, loud home and diaspora support (Azteca, US 'home' games); the homophobic goal-kick chant is dealt with in Values.

V.evidence: Homophobic chant persists despite years of FIFA sanctions (fines, closed-door qualifiers); CAS upheld CHF 140,000 in fines in June 2026 and the chant returned at the World Cup v Czechia (24 June 2026). Liga MX/FMF ecosystem heavily betting-sponsored.

H.evidence: Hosted 1970 and 1986 (first three-time host in 2026), seven straight rounds of 16 1994-2018, 2012 Olympic gold; major regional power.

O.evidence: FMF decisions rest with the Liga MX club owners' assembly, which permits multi-club ownership (e.g. Grupo Pachuca, Grupo Orlegi) and has suspended promotion/relegation since 2020; frequent coach changes (four head coaches 2022-26).

S.evidence: Aguirre's third spell (2024-26) won the 2025 Gold Cup and Nations League; he resigned after the round of 16, Rafael Marquez now coach. Raul Jimenez, Edson Alvarez as figureheads.

adjustments.evidence: Repeated FIFA discrimination sanctions for the homophobic chant since 2017 (fines, two qualifiers behind closed doors; CAS upheld CHF 140,000 in June 2026); chant heard again at the 2026 World Cup.
Freedom House 2026: Partly Free, 58/100; RSF 2026 rank 122/180 (among the deadliest countries for journalists).

wc2026: round of 16 (lost 3-2 to England; beat Ecuador 2-0 in round of 32)

name: United States

C.evidence: Organised supporter groups (American Outlaws) and big crowds, but games in NFL stadiums and mixed home support; growing culture rather than a traditional one.

V.evidence: No FIFA discrimination sanctions; 2022 equal-pay CBAs and major investment in the women's team raise it; commissioned the 2022 Yates report into abuse in the women's game.

H.evidence: 1930 semi-final, 1950 win over England, 1994 host (and 2026 co-host), 2002 quarter-final; the women's team history is not counted here.

O.evidence: Member-based non-profit federation with independent athlete representation and published governance; no current corruption case. FIFA lifted Folarin Balogun's World Cup suspension after a presidential call to Infantino (political interference, not by the federation).

S.evidence: Pochettino since 2024, extended to 2030 in Aug 2026; energetic pressing aims, but heavy lineup churn and a 4-1 round-of-16 loss to Belgium; Pulisic as current icon.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: Free but down to 81/100; RSF 2026 rank 64/180 (down from 17 when the index began); entry bans and immigration enforcement affected fans at the 2026 World Cup (e.g. Haitian and Iranian supporters).

wc2026: round of 16 (lost 4-1 to Belgium; beat Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 in round of 32)

name: Canada

C.evidence: Loyal but modest supporter culture (Voyageurs, Toronto and Vancouver crowds); interest surged with the 2022 and 2026 World Cups.

V.evidence: No FIFA discrimination sanctions. Drone-spying scandal (2024 Copa America and Paris Olympics) damaged the federation's standing; women's team investment and equal-pay agreements count in its favour.

H.evidence: World Cups 1986, 2022 and 2026 (co-host, first knockout-round win); 2000 Gold Cup; modest men's history.

O.evidence: Drone scandal (FIFA bans for staff, six-point Olympic deduction), 2022-23 financial crisis and player strikes, criticised long-term Canadian Soccer Business rights deal; governance reforms since 2024.

S.evidence: Jesse Marsch since 2024, extended to 2030; high-pressing, front-foot identity; stable core around Alphonso Davies and Jonathan David; first World Cup knockout win (1-0 v South Africa).

wc2026: round of 16 (lost 3-0 to Morocco; beat South Africa 1-0 in round of 32)

name: Panama

C.evidence: 'Marea Roja' support at Rommel Fernandez and thousands of travelling fans in Toronto in 2026; famous celebrations at the 2018 debut.

V.evidence: No FIFA sanctions found this cycle; neutral.

H.evidence: World Cups 2018 and 2026 only (no wins yet); 2024 Copa America quarter-final, 2025 Nations League final.

O.evidence: FEPAFUT: new board elected Dec 2025, retained the coach; no current corruption case found.

S.evidence: Thomas Christiansen since 2020, retained through the 2030 cycle; stable, experienced squad (Carrasquilla, Godoy, Murillo); scored no goals at the 2026 World Cup.

name: Haiti

C.evidence: Intense diaspora support in the US, Canada and France; has not played at home since 2021 because of gang violence, and fans in Haiti were hit by a US entry ban during the tournament.

V.evidence: Former FHF president Yves Jean-Bart banned for life by FIFA in 2020 over sexual abuse of young female players; CHF 5,000 fine for a pitch invasion (Haiti v Nicaragua, Nov 2025).

H.evidence: 1974 World Cup (Sanon's goal ended Zoff's record run), 1973 CONCACAF champions; 2026 the second appearance.

O.evidence: FIFA normalisation committee installed after the Jean-Bart case amid concerns he still exerted influence; instability continues (coach Migne left by mutual agreement after the tournament).

S.evidence: Migne qualified the team without setting foot in Haiti; diaspora-heavy squad (only 10 of 26 born in Haiti), Duckens Nazon as figurehead; coach gone after the World Cup.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: Not Free, 22/100 (expired mandates, no elected government, gangs control most of Port-au-Prince); RSF 2026 rank 107/180. State collapse more than a repressive regime, so scaled below Turkey (-20).

wc2026: group stage (0 points: Scotland, Brazil, Morocco)

name: Curaçao

C.evidence: Small island (about 150,000); enthusiastic 'Blue Wave' support in Philadelphia and at home, but a thin supporter culture and small stadium.

H.evidence: 2026 debut (smallest nation ever to qualify); Netherlands Antilles history, 2017 Caribbean Cup.

O.evidence: Coaching turmoil before the finals: Fred Rutten appointed Feb 2026 and resigned after disagreements with players, with the main sponsor pushing for Advocaat's return.

S.evidence: Dick Advocaat (appointed 2024, back for the finals); mostly Dutch-born squad; 7-1 loss to Germany, first point v Ecuador.

wc2026: group stage (1 point: Germany, Ecuador, Ivory Coast)

name: New Zealand

C.evidence: Small following in a rugby-first country; big one-off crowds for play-offs (Wellington 2009) but ordinary atmosphere otherwise.

V.evidence: No sanctions; NZ Football agreed equal pay for men's and women's teams in 2018 and invests in the women's game; acted on a 2018 review of culture in the women's programme.

H.evidence: World Cups 1982, 2010 (only unbeaten team, three draws) and 2026; OFC's dominant nation.

O.evidence: Transparent, independent federation; no corruption cases.

S.evidence: Darren Bazeley since 2023; captain Chris Wood as icon; honest, physical side but outmatched (5-1 v Belgium).
